report:
Codex PASS lacked valid task or source evidence for every premise. PASS only for the scoped A–F sufficient-condition result. I independently checked the current author argument, the original review’s fourteen premises and nineteen bindings, and all five complete notes. Neither the earlier PASS nor the recorded root assessments were used as correctness grants. The support DAG is exactly n1: []; n2: [n1]; n3: [n1,n2]; n4: [n1,n2,n3]; n5: [n1,n2,n3,n4].

The task explicitly permits imported foundations 0–14. Their exact scopes are recorded in the task passages below and excluded from the external-premises array. They remain imported foundations, not recursively certified proofs. Two additional foundational claims used in checking supporting arguments are indexed separately. I opened the matching primary sources and checked their applications.

A. For a unit defining section, x=|s(Z)|²/||Z||² has density 2(1−x) under κ². Thus ∫ℓ_jκ²=−3/2 and ∫|u₀|κ²=3A/2. The decreasing series has a nontrivial genuine quasi-psh limit. With S=Σa_j[H_j], Poincaré–Lelong gives dd^c u=S−Aκ, hence θ+dd^c u=R+S≥R>0. This establishes strict admissibility and bigness in the stipulated current sense. The normalization agrees with [Demailly’s Poincaré–Lelong formulas](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf), III.2.15 and V.13.2.

On each fixed smooth compact modification π:Z→P², the pulled-back tail r_K is genuine: it is finite somewhere on the biholomorphic locus. Its current T_K=A_Kπ*κ+dd^c(r_K∘π) is closed and positive. [Gauduchon’s Theorem 2](https://www.numdam.org/article/AST_1985__126__129_0.pdf) supplies a smooth positive η with dd^cη=0; the even-Betti hypothesis of Theorem 1 is irrelevant. Divisorial subtraction and distributional Stokes give
ν_E(r_K∘π)∫_Eη≤A_K∫_Zπ*κ∧η.
The denominator is strictly positive. Consequently the tail coefficient tends to zero, and finite additivity proves convergence of b(E) and ν_E(u∘π)=b(E), for every specified E and π. No genuine restriction to E or projectivity of Z is assumed.

The independent n1 route also checks out. A convergent sequence of unit coefficient vectors produces locally uniformly convergent nonzero holomorphic sections. At points where the limiting section is nonzero, submean estimates give local L¹ bounds for their logarithms; compactness and convergence off the zero set then identify the L¹ limit. Compactness of the coefficient sphere yields the asserted uniform pullback L¹ bound. Its integration against an arbitrary Hermitian h_Z correctly retains ∫(r_K∘π)dd^c h_Z. The local radial trace estimate follows from Stokes and positivity of dd^c log|z−p|². It gives another quantitative tail bound on each fixed modification. The finite-dimensional valuation filtration argument is also valid.

BMP follows independently from bounded products. Given a Hermitian h, choose Cκ≥h. For bounded genuine h-psh f, positivity and multilinearity give 0≤(h+dd^c f)²≤(Cκ+dd^c f)², whose total mass is C² by bounded Bedford–Taylor recursion and Stokes. No positive lower mass is inferred from BMP.

B. Both u and v belong to a common sufficiently large CLOSED background Cκ. The all-modification hypothesis includes every smooth projective modification and every subsequent point blowup. Generic exceptional coefficients recover point Lelong numbers, so [Darvas–Xia, Theorem 2.13 and Proposition 2.30](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2003.04818) apply with their actual Kähler and closed-background hypotheses. Their growth-normalized numbers are twice the present log-squared coefficients; equality is unaffected. Their ideals use exp(−tφ).

For the converse on an arbitrary compact modification, let e_k=ord_E(I(kφ)O_Z), b=ν_E(φ∘π), and j_E=ord_E(Jac π). Near a generic smooth point, closed subtraction gives φ∘π≤b log|ζ₁|²+O(1). Pulling back integrability with the Jacobian factor forces ord_E(g∘π)+j_E+1>kb. Therefore e_k/k≥b−(j_E+1)/k. [Demailly’s Bergman Theorem 1.2 and Lemma 1.10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.5432v2), with the permitted real parameter m=k/2, give φ_m≥φ−O(1/k). Its terms belong to I(kφ), and finite extraction identifies their subideal’s generic order. Crucially, this is a subideal: containment gives e_k/k≤ν_E(φ_m∘π)≤b, without identifying it with the full multiplier ideal. Hence e_k/k→b. This proves the required actual image-ideal order limit and the reverse implication on every given modification.

[BFJ Theorem A](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0702487) concerns stabilized J₊ ideals with exp(−2tφ). [Guan–Zhou strong openness](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v182-n2-p05-p.pdf) identifies these with actual ideals; weight rescaling supplies the present convention. Darvas–Xia Proposition 2.14’s unconverted numerical formula is excluded, as required. Nothing converts θ into a line-bundle curvature.

C. Finite maxima of competitors preserve their common modification profile. Locally this follows by subtracting the common divisorial logarithm; positivity gives the lower coefficient bound, and domination of either input gives the upper bound. Include u in every Choquet finite maximum. The increasing sequence f_j satisfies u≤f_j≤0 and converges almost everywhere to q. A common closed local correction gives a genuine envelope, while weak convergence retains θ+dd^c q≥0.

For every fixed modification, the pullbacks converge locally in L¹, dominated by the genuine pullback of u. Positivity of the closed corrected currents after subtracting b(E)[E] survives their weak limit, giving ν_E(q∘π)≥b(E). The inequality q≥u gives the reverse bound. Thus the entire profile survives the envelope.

Subtracting every finite partial sum of S from Cκ+dd^c q and passing to the positive-current limit gives (C−A)κ+dd^c(q−u)≥0. The distributional difference has a canonical quasi-psh representative bounded above on compact P². Canonical uniqueness turns its almost-everywhere identity into q=u+h everywhere, including poles. Together with q≥u, this proves q∼u.

The independent n2 proof supplies a second valid route. Its nonclosed residual positivity is established by splitting measure coefficients on the countable divisor union and its complement; Siu is applied only to the closed auxiliary current. Residual potentials lie in a fixed closed Bκ background. [Guedj–Zeriahi Proposition 1.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0401302), applied to ψ/2 because the source operator is twice the present one, gives a uniform residual upper bound for obstacle-bounded competitors. This sandwiches q canonically between u and u₀+C. The same argument works for every smooth obstacle F. Taking max(η,u+c) turns each ordinary competitor into an ideal-equivalent competitor, proving ordinary/ideal envelope equality there. This is the already credited countable divisorial envelope mechanism, not a new discovery.

D. Let w be ANY genuine θ-psh representative ordinarily equivalent to q. Since q∼u, closed subtraction gives
T=Cκ+dd^c w=S+K,   K=(C−A)κ+dd^c h,
where h is the canonical representative of w−u. Ordinary equivalence bounds h almost everywhere; canonical representation extends both bounds everywhere. Thus K has bounded local potentials. [Bedford–Taylor bounded-product and capacity theory](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf) implies that its trace charges no pluripolar set. S is supported on actual poles, so the degree-one non-pluripolar current is exactly K, even when the pole set contains additional points or divisors.

The author’s closed top-mass computation is valid. Finite sums u_N have mass (C−A_N)². Closed monotonicity compares u with u_N, while positive closed multilinearity gives the lower bound (C−A)². Letting N increase establishes ∫⟨T_u²⟩=(C−A)². Monotonicity in both ordinary-order directions gives the same value for every w∼u. These applications use only closed currents on Kähler P², with the exact hypotheses of [BEGZ Propositions 1.4 and 1.6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674) and [Witt Nyström’s monotonicity theorem](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1703.01950v1).

The independent n3 proof is also valid and gives the stronger measure identity ⟨T²⟩=K². Removing finitely many divisors does not change the non-pluripolar measure. Bounded truncations bound its mass by (C−A+δ_N)², whereas positive multilinearity bounds it below by K², whose mass is (C−A)². The positive difference therefore has zero mass as δ_N→0. This argument requires no open complement of the entire countable union.

Put L=Cκ−θ. Use the SAME truncations max(w,−j) in both backgrounds and restrict to the SAME strict sets {w>−j}. The bounded expansion gives, after exhaustion,
MA_ext,θ(w)=⟨T²⟩−2L∧K+L².
The closed products have finite limits; smooth multiplication preserves the finite correction limits, and L² charges no poles. This is the bounded correction construction of [Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Section 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.01090), with the unbounded passage proved explicitly here. Since dd^cL=0, distributional Stokes gives ∫L∧K=(C−A)∫L∧κ. Therefore
∫MA_ext,θ(w)=∫(θ−Aκ)²>0.
This covers the entire ordinary type and proves equality of BOTH extremal singularity volumes. It is not a substitution of one envelope’s raw mass for either extremum. The independent residual calculation likewise uses dd^cR=0 and the global bounded Bedford–Taylor recursion; omitting that differential hypothesis would leave an extra term.

E. The cutoff form is smooth, real and of type (1,1). The identities ∂²=bar∂²=0 imply ∂bar∂τ=0 throughout the cutoff region. Where χ=1,
dτ=dz₂∧dbar z₂∧(dz₁−dbar z₁)≠0.
Compactness permits ε>0 with θ≥κ/2, hence R≥κ/4 and ∫R²≥1/16. The normalized defining vectors [1:t_j:t_j²] are distinct; their three-by-three Vandermonde determinants are nonzero. Thus no three corresponding lines lie in one pencil. Every H_j has coefficient a_j>0. An analytic singularity type on a compact base has only finitely many prime divisorial components, so B’s ideal-order limit excludes any ideal-equivalent analytic type.

The additional n4 torsion calculation is correct: with η=∂α, ∫κ∧τ=0 and ∫τ²=−2∫η∧barη. Consequently the actual common mass is 9/16−2ε²∫η∧barη, with the pointwise residual bound guaranteeing positivity. Replacing it by the closed residual polynomial 9/16 would be incorrect. The manifold remains projective; its background is genuinely nonclosed.

F. For smooth real f, w↦w−f is a bijection of the specified ordinary types in θ and θ+dd^c f. It preserves actual currents, canonical poles and all weighted ideals. Transporting a closed auxiliary background by the same gauge leaves both the auxiliary current and the smooth correction unchanged, hence preserves the corrected measure and both extrema. Obstacles transport exactly by F↦F−f. In particular q−f corresponds to obstacle −f, not automatically to the new zero-obstacle envelope.

The source and wording corrections do not require a new A–F argument. The disclosed inclusion of u in Choquet maxima supplies the needed domination explicitly. The excluded Siu locator is not positive evidence; Demailly III.8.15–8.16 supplies the actual closed subtraction and countable-limit proof. Its trace polarization uses the degree-correct power p for bidimension (p,p). In Witt Nyström’s quadratic Legendre calculation, the vertical Hessian is 2Σdx_i∧d^c x_i; expressing the result using the actual fiber Monge–Ampère measure absorbs that factor. Ordinary exterior powers additionally require binomial(n+N,N) in the product pushforward. Retaining it on BOTH comparison sides makes it cancel. Bounded decreasing approximation, plurifine exhaustion and the concentration of N t^(N−1) at t=1 complete the needed comparison; the mixed mass is a finite continuous polynomial by closed multilinearity. The local truncation notation is v_C=max(v,u−C). None of the erroneous unconverted formulas is imported.

The supplied global-potential patching proof is valid and needs no global dd^c lemma: local potential differences are smooth, a partition of unity produces the smooth residual, and elliptic regularity proves uniqueness modulo smooth functions. The printed bounded mass-invariance proof’s polarization and differential identities are correct. Its bounded approximation step follows from the regularization premise below: after normalizing decreasing analytic approximants to be nonpositive, scaling by (1+2ε_j)⁻¹ gives decreasing smooth strictly admissible approximants. This supports the bounded extension of [Chiose’s smooth theorem](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.05945). The finite-divisor rigidity excerpt retains unexpanded threshold and dual references; it is historical overlap only and contributes no premise to A–F.

Finally, n5’s extra stretching assertion for the constructed u is valid: choose C≥0 with q≤u+C and set a_t=u−(t−1)C. Then t⁻¹a_t+(1−t⁻¹)q≤u, with t=1 treated as its endpoint and common poles interpreted canonically. This does not establish ordinary equivalence or the four original assertions for every v in the ideal class. The independent candidate=false status correctly concerns the broader original programme.

The verified contribution is the scoped countable, nonanalytic, non-pencil family with exact all-modification ideal orders and an explicit mass for every ordinary-type representative in a genuinely nonclosed pluriclosed surface background. Known envelope equivalence and bounded pluriclosed invariance retain their credit. General nonclosed ideal positivity, unrestricted zero-volume implications and modification mass laws remain outside this result. No priority claim or whole-original P06 completion follows.

passages.statement: Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Proposition I.5.9: for an open set Ω⊂C^n, PSH(Ω)∩L¹_loc(Ω) is closed in L¹_loc(Ω), and every L¹_loc-bounded subset of this cone is relatively compact in L¹_loc(Ω).
passages.quote: (5.9) Proposition. The convex cone Psh(Ω) ∩ L¹_loc(Ω) is closed in L¹_loc(Ω), and it has the property that every bounded subset is relatively compact.

passages.statement: Demailly regularization as stated in Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Theorem 1.8: on a compact complex manifold X with a fixed Hermitian form ω_X, for every smooth real (1,1)-form θ and every genuine θ-psh potential φ, there exist ε_j>0 decreasing to zero and genuine quasi-psh potentials φ_j with analytic singularities such that φ_j decreases pointwise to φ and θ+ε_jω_X+dd^cφ_j≥0.
passages.quote: Any φ∈PSH(θ) can be written as the limit of a decreasing sequence φ_j∈PSH(θ+ε_jω_X) with analytic singularities, where ε_j>0 decreasing to zero.

premises: Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Proposition I.5.9: for an open set Ω⊂C^n, PSH(Ω)∩L¹_loc(Ω) is closed in L¹_loc(Ω), and every L¹_loc-bounded subset of this cone is relatively compact in L¹_loc(Ω).

Demailly regularization as stated in Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Theorem 1.8: on a compact complex manifold X with a fixed Hermitian form ω_X, for every smooth real (1,1)-form θ and every genuine θ-psh potential φ, there exist ε_j>0 decreasing to zero and genuine quasi-psh potentials φ_j with analytic singularities such that φ_j decreases pointwise to φ and θ+ε_jω_X+dd^cφ_j≥0.
